n.story:
Your role is transitioning from a hands-on technician to a high-level biological systems architect. In the past, you spent hours manually grading fish, checking water chemistry, and monitoring pump speeds. Now, computer vision systems and IoT sensors handle the constant stream of data, identifying species and health anomalies in real-time. This automation doesn't replace you; it frees you to focus on the complex 'why' behind the data, such as predicting disease outbreaks before they occur or optimizing water reuse cycles for maximum sustainability.

You will spend more of your time designing sophisticated fish welfare plans and managing the delicate balance of biofilter ecosystems. While AI handles the routine adjustments of the recirculation systems, your expertise is required for high-stakes troubleshooting and the physical maintenance that keeps the facility running. Your value lies in your ability to synthesize scientific data into actionable strategies that ensure both regulatory compliance and optimal growth rates.
